intro.title: Build typed normalization for entities
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed normalization system for entity data, such as users or products, using TypeScript. You'll learn to transform an array of objects into a normalized structure with separate `ids` and `entities` objects, making data access more efficient. The core concept involves using TypeScript generics and interfaces to enforce type safety throughout the normalization process. You'll work with key TypeScript constructs like `Record` and `Pick` to define and manipulate types. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe normalization function that ensures your data is consistently structured and easy to manage.
intro.usecase: Typed normalization is essential in applications with complex data relationships, like e-commerce platforms where products have categories, reviews, and inventory data. In dashboards displaying user analytics, normalization ensures consistent user profiles across charts, tables, and filters. When building social media feeds with posts, comments, and reactions, typed normalization prevents data duplication and maintains type safety during updates. This pattern is also crucial in form builders with reusable field components, where normalized schemas guarantee data integrity across nested sections.
